hints: Look at the structure of butan-2-one and check for the methyl ketone group that gives a positive iodoform test.
Remember the iodoform cleavage splits off the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ part as $\text{CHI}_3$, leaving the rest of the molecule as a carboxylate ion in alkali.
Think about what excess dilute acid does to a carboxylate ion, it protonates it to the neutral acid form.
walkthrough:
**Spot the iodoform reaction**

This is the classic triiodomethane (iodoform) test for a methyl ketone. Butan-2-one is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, so it contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group.

General rule:
$$\text{RCOCH}_3 + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 + \text{RCOO}^- + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Find the first organic product in alkali**

Here $\text{R}$ is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-$. The $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ fragment becomes $\text{CHI}_3$, and the remaining fragment becomes the carboxylate.

For this ketone:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-$$
So in alkaline solution product M starts as propanoate ion.

**Account for the acid addition**

An excess of dilute sulfuric acid is then added. This provides $\text{H}^+$ ions which protonate any carboxylate ion to the carboxylic acid.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^- + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
So the final isolated organic product M alongside $\text{CHI}_3$ is propanoic acid.

options.A: Incorrect. Ethanoate ion, $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$, would form from butan-2-one only if the ethyl fragment was lost as $\text{CHI}_3$, which is impossible because $\text{CHI}_3$ must come from the methyl group. Also, an ion cannot survive after excess acid is added.
options.B: Incorrect. Ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, has only 2 carbons. Butan-2-one has 4 carbons and $\text{CHI}_3$ accounts for only 1 carbon from the methyl group, so the other fragment must contain 3 carbons, not 2.
options.C: Incorrect trap. Propanoate ion, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-$, is indeed formed in the first alkaline step, but the question asks after excess dilute sulfuric acid is added. The acid protonates the ion, so you no longer have the ion in the final mixture.
options.D: Correct. The alkaline iodoform cleavage of $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ gives $\text{CHI}_3$ plus propanoate ion, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-$. Excess $\text{H}^+$ then protonates it to propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, which is the final product M.
